config.title: How to Read a Berlin Address - FAQ
config.subtitle: Simple address checks for getting to the right Berlin street, building and entrance.

items.q: What order should a Berlin address use?
items.a: Keep the street name and house number together, then the five-digit postcode and Berlin. If a booking includes a courtyard, entrance, floor or bell note, keep that with the address as well.

items.q: Does the letter after a Berlin house number matter?
items.a: Yes. Treat a letter such as 12a as part of the exact number, not as optional punctuation. Preserve any letter, range or slash from the original address when you search or give the address to someone.

items.q: Do I need to know which Berlin district a postcode belongs to?
items.a: No. Use the five-digit postcode as a confirmation that your map and booking describe the same place. You do not need to memorise the district before you go.

items.q: Can I use odd and even house numbers to find the right side of a Berlin street?
items.a: Sometimes, but not as a universal rule. Berlin has older streets with horseshoe numbering as well as the more familiar zig-zag pattern, so follow the exact number in your map and at the building.

items.q: What should I do with a Berlin address that includes Hof or Aufgang?
items.a: Keep that note attached to the street address until you arrive. It is useful arrival information that may distinguish the correct courtyard, stairway or entrance after you have reached the building.
